references.text: One-tenth of an ephah is the same measure as an omer, which was used to measure manna in the wilderness.
The same regulation for a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil for the grain offering accompanying the daily burnt offering.
Refers to pure, beaten olive oil (שֶׁמֶן כָּתִית) that was to be used in the sanctuary.
Basic regulation for a grain offering (מִנְחָה) of fine flour (סֹלֶת) with oil.
Describes a grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, the same ingredients as in Num 28:5.
Prescribes one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as the daily grain offering, divided between morning and evening.
Refers to pure, beaten olive oil (שֶׁמֶן כָּתִית) for the lamp in the sanctuary.
The same amount of fine flour (one-tenth of an ephah) and oil (a quarter of a hin) for the grain offering accompanying the burnt offering.
Ezekiel's description of the daily grain offering with fine flour and oil in the future temple.
